questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to use a phone app to count calories and lose weight
Why going to the gym is boring for most adults
The best places to walk in the UK in the summer
Whether adults exercise enough and how to walk more
questions.why: Rob says they're discussing vigorous exercise and whether adults take enough of it.

questions.q: What does Neil say about his own walking?
options: He tracks his steps and does 10,000 a day
He only walks at weekends, in the countryside
He never counts his steps because it's boring
He walks slowly every evening to relax
questions.why: Neil says you can track steps on your phone and he does ten thousand a day.

questions.q: Why does Rob joke about walking from the sofa to the fridge?
options: To show that he walks much more than Neil every day
To explain how he counts his steps with his phone
To suggest slow, short walks aren't real exercise
To say that he is always hungry in the evenings
questions.why: Rob says 10,000 steps don't count 'if you saunter', like from the sofa to the fridge.

questions.q: According to Neil, what happens to your body when you exercise?
options: You need less sleep at night and wake up earlier
It stimulates its repair system and stays younger
You get much hungrier and so you eat more food
Your heart beats more slowly for the rest of the day
questions.why: Neil says exercise stimulates the body's natural repair system, so it stays younger.

questions.q: What excuse does Rob give for not walking more?
options: He has a bad knee
He is far too busy
He lives too far from a park
He doesn't like walking alone
questions.why: Rob says he doesn't have enough time because he's 'far too busy'.

questions.q: How does Julia Bradbury build walking into her working day?
options: She goes to the gym for an hour every day before work
She runs in the park near her office at lunchtime
She walks around the office for five minutes every hour
She walks to meetings rather than take a bus or taxi
questions.why: She says she will walk to meetings instead of catching a bus or getting a taxi or car.

questions.q: What does Julia do on days at home with her children?
options: She walks with them for at least 30–40 minutes
She takes them swimming
She stays in and does exercise videos
She drives them to the park
questions.why: She takes her kids out in the buggy and does '30-40 minutes at least every day'.

questions.q: How does Rob respond to Julia's ideas?
options: He says they wouldn't work for him because of his job
He thinks she has too much free time to be realistic
He agrees he could walk, not drive, and take the stairs
He says he already does all of them every single day
questions.why: Rob says she walks instead of driving and takes the stairs, and 'I could do those things'.
